source: Next
I see you're wasting no time asserting yourself, Clarissa.
The service is over. Just getting people out.
These people don't care about him anyway.
They were in my way.
And does that deny them the right to mourn him?
I suppose not.
It denies them the pretense of caring.
...Where's my dad?

They care, Clarissa. Just not in the same way you and I do - the way family does. Your grandfather was important enough to make Great Apes pay attention. No, they care about what he represented more than who he was.
We may be family, but I think we knew him differently too.
We both know family can mean very different things, Clemence.
They're playing it up now, but in a few days they'll act like he never existed. It's not fair.
Carlo is going to be the leader of the family now, Clarissa. I'm sure he had to go tend to certain matters.
...Certain matters that I'm still not allowed to know of.
"Certain matters." I'm not a child, Clemence.
That isn't fair.
I know you feel alone, Clarissa, but \r\ngrief is communal. The life he knew all these people in wasn't one you were part of.
Am I supposed to be thankful for that?
I'm not a child, Clemence. I know what you're talking about.
That life is still around, but the one we had is gone. It's not fair.
No. You should take your time. Hurrying grief does you no favors.
It's hard to focus on it around all these strangers.
These people seem to do neither.
It looks like my dad disagrees with you.
I know, Clarissa. I do, too.
I feel lost without him.
Can we leave? I can't stand all these people pretending to care.
Have you seen Dad?
Listen, Clarissa, your grandfather wanted certain things for you. A different life, one that you'd choose. Something other than this one.
You don't seem very sad, Uncle.
How are you dealing with all this?
I know what you're talking about, yet I don't think you do.
You don't seem very sad, Uncle.
How are you dealing with all this?
Not much is fair, Clarisssa.
You don't seem very sad, Uncle.
How are you dealing with all this?
Ah, I don't know if I am dealing with all this...change. Not just yet, anyway.
I'm sorry.
You should take some time for yourself.
So would you want to?
Being clever isn't enough, Clarissa. Planning is what gives you the upper edge. Foreseeing contingencies. You do this, I do this. They do that, I do that.
I already do that, Uncle.
Are you going to teach me?
I prefer to improvise.
There's a lot in motion right now. Gaps to be filled, scores to be settled. Doesn't leave me with much time to myself, or my own thoughts.
I'm sorry. That must be hard.
You should take some time for yourself.
That's a convenient excuse to not process things.
You. Sneaking around the altar, checking the collection box. Very clever.
Just misdirection. Nothing fancy.
Sneaking? Me?
There wasn't much in there, anyway.
Ah, right. Of course I didn't. How much was in that collection box, by the way?
I didn't check. The important part was drawing attention to it.
More than you'd think, but less than you'd hope.
However much it was, it wasn't enough for the priest.
So you made the priest speak up instead. Very clever.
Just needed to push the right buttons. Nothing fancy.
I just asked a couple questions, that's all.
Guess whatever was in the collection box wasn't enough.
And what if someone had caught wind of what you were doing?
I'd have improvised.
What if they had?
No one did.
Don't be coy. It doesn't suit you, nor the occasion.
If anything, it makes it easier to deal with all this.
Relax. I'm too smart for these people anyway.
I'm kidding. Everything's fine, Uncle. No one saw me, anyway.
12 loons. I know,  because I put them there.
I didn't take you for the religious type.
Sure. Point is, no one saw me do anything.
How generous of you.
I did, didn't I?
Listen, I can handle myself.
So you'll always be around, keeping an eye on me?
You're different.
If you say so. Next time, you just come find me and I'll sort it out for you. Alright?
I can manage myself just fine.
Is this your way of saying you want to spend more time with me?
Sure. As long as we figure it out together.
I don't doubt it. I just worry.
Aren't there bigger things to worry about?
What about you? How are you dealing with all this?
Could be. Your father is going to be a busy man, and someone's got to look after you.
I don't need a babysitter.
Things are going to change, aren't they?
How about you? How are you dealing with all this?
I'll bear that in mind.
What else is on your mind?
You worry too much, Uncle. How are you dealing with all this?
These are acquaintances of your grandfather - many of them powerful people.
I don't care.
Then I just show them I'm no different.
Then they should understand how I'm feeling.
No. But it's important to know when to speak up, not just how. This was not the time.
Who gives a shit. I don't care what they think, anyway.
They don't get to decide that.
No, this was exactly the time. I was closer to him than any of them.
I could see that. I'd be annoyed, too. But those people are going to remember that.
I don't care what they think.
What, I should wait politely?
It's Grandpa's funeral. Of course I'm a little on edge.
You should. You don't have to like, or even respect them. But you should care. And know who they are.
And feed their egos? No thank you.
When they return the favor, I will.
Fine. Doesn't mean I have to like it.
I'm sure they'll take notice once you grow up. In more ways than one.
How do you deal with all this?
Doesn't it get to you? All of this?
No, it doesn't. And I'm sorry about that.
Not your fault. How do you deal with all this?
Doesn't it get to you? All of this?
The game is old as time, Clarissa. If you want to beat them, you have to play along.
Is that how you deal with all this?
Doesn't it get to you? All of this?
Listen, I don't want to lecture you, especially after a sermon like that. But standing your ground is not the same thing as enforcing your will.
It should be. That'd be simpler.
Whatever. I just need them to stay out of my way.
Earn their respect, but on their terms? That doesn't seem fair.
Ah, they won't offer you that level of understanding. To them, you're just a kid. Regardless of who your grandfather was.
Well, they're wrong.
I'll show them. They'll see.
Doesn't seem very fair, does it?
Don't you worry about me, sweetie. You've got plenty on your own plate. Keep a level head and focus on that.
So what's going to happen now?
What did you think of the funeral?
Hah - if only it were as easy as you make it sound! No, Clarissa - myself and the family are synonymous. What the family does, I do. That's how it's always been.
So what's going to happen now?
What did you make of the funeral?
I miss your grandfather. But things are about to change and very soon. Whether that will be for the better remains to be seen.
So what's going to happen now?
So what did you make of the funeral?
Now? Well, your father is going to be in charge. Which means a whole new set of palms to grease and a score of opportunists that will need to be pacified.
Pacified?
Don't they have any respect?
(CUNNING) I see. If there's space to be filled, some will be happy to hide in the corners.

Very somber, very traditional. I'm afraid I can't participate as much as I'd like, or should, in occasions like this. Business will always be business. We live and die, but throughout all of it, there's always someone who stands to gain something.
(AMBITIOUS) So we'll need to be on top of things.
Is that what you're doing? Trying to gain something?
At a funeral? Fucking vultures.
No, bella. I make sure no one gains something they ought not to. I look after interests of the family.
Speaking of family, where is my father?
I wish you didn't have to.
A body is a body, I'm afraid.
[Shake your head] Where's my father?
Is that what this life is?
We'll need to keep them at bay. Happy enough to back off, but not happy enough to get any ideas. See what I'm saying?
I do. Speaking of my father, where is he?
Is that how it's going to be from now on? Grandpa's gone, and our life just turns into...crowd control?
Not like they used to. In the old days, respect was paramount. Now it's starting to become performative.
...Where's my father?
Is that how it's going to be from now on? Grandpa's gone, and life just turns into...this?
Clarissa, bella. You're not going to make many friends acting like that.
They were in my way.
I don't care about these idiots.
Do you have a problem with me speaking up, Uncle?
That's right. If nothing else, that much is predictable.
Where's my father, by the way?
Is that how it's going to be from now on? Grandpa's gone, and life just turns into...watching our backs?
I do. For now, you take this time for yourself, Clarissa. Focus on yourself, and the family.
Speaking of family, where is my father?
Family just seems like business now.
Outside. Said there were things he needed to deal with. I don't doubt it.
(AMBITIOUS) His own plans, I'm sure.
(CUNNING) Is that the change you were talking about, Uncle?
(POWERFUL) Well, I fucking do. I need to talk to him.
What? When did he leave?
It's not so bad, Clarissa. It's far from an easy life, but then again, what easy life is worth living?
Where's my father?
(AMBITIOUS) I don't want an easy life. I just want a life of my own.
(CUNNING) Easy is as easy does. I'm sure I could combine the two.
(POWERFUL) Damn right. If you want something out of life, you have to claim it yourself.
Could be. He will be running the family, Clarissa. You'll need to...show him more respect.
Oh, I'll show him something.
And when did he leave?
Some of it, for certain. Give him time, Clarissa. He has a lot to deal with right now.
He's about to have even more.
When did he leave?
[Sigh] Fine.
...Clarissa.
I need to talk to him. Now.
When did he leave?
I understand that. I hope by the Shepherd that one day you'll have that choice, and I hope Carlo will make sure of it.
Speaking of my father, I want to talk to him before we go.
[Say nothing]
I'm sure you will. For now, let's go. There's still tradition to attend to.
Let me find my father first. I need to talk to him.
[Sigh] I suppose so.
Maybe so. You tend to take what you can get, bella. For now, let's go. There's still things we need to see to.
I need to talk to my father first.
Not very keen on talking to a bunch of more strangers.
I saw that, you know.
Saw what?
[Shrug] I wanted to keep things quiet.
No, you didn't.
At some point during the sermon. He went outside, but I think he's probably still around.
I want to talk to him.
[Say nothing]
Ah, I'm not sure that now is a good time. You should save it for later, Clarissa.
No. I need to talk to him.
Fine.
...Come on. I'll get the car ready. Take your time, and meet me outside. I'll drive you to the reception.
Thank you.
[Nod]
We'll see. Not sure I can handle the reception as well.
... And I don't think you should. I'll see you outside.
I don't care.
[Say nothing]
I'll see you there.
Usually, funerals like these have more of a slow burn to them. Gives us time to reflect on your grandfather's life.
These people didn't know him.
I just want it to be over.
I don't want time to reflect. I want time with him.
That's unfair, Clarissa. Many of them knew your grandfather. They were colleagues, friends.
They didn't know him the way I did.
I don't have time for them. I want them out.
I just wish it was just us here. Just family.
I see.
They didn't know him the way I did, Clemence.
I just need to go outside. Clear my head.
[Stare at him]
